title: Trust and Adoption Intention Toward AI-Enabled IBM Cloud Services Among IT Professionals in Bangladesh
content: Artificial-intelligence-enabled cloud services are becoming increasingly important for digital transformation, but users may not adopt these services simply because they believe the technology is useful. This study examines the factors associated with adoption intention toward AI-enabled IBM Cloud services in Bangladesh, with particular attention to performance expectations, trust, technology readiness and digital skills readiness. The analysis uses the Group 5 survey database, which contains 400 records. After applying the prespecified attention-check criterion, 385 cases were retained for the main analysis. The database contains 30 five-point Likert-scale items representing 10 constructs: perceived usefulness, relative advantage, compatibility, innovation adoption readiness, performance expectancy, effort expectancy, trust, technology readiness, digital skills readiness and adoption intention. Descriptive statistics, reliability and measurement diagnostics, hierarchical regression, bootstrap analysis and importance-performance analysis were used to examine the data. Overall adoption intention was positive (M=3.79, SD=0.48). The full regression model explained 30.5% of the variance in adoption intention. Technology readiness was the strongest unique predictor (β=.224, p<.001), followed by performance expectancy (β=.157, p=.001), digital skills readiness (β=.147, p=.002) and trust (β=.140, p=.003). Adding the trust and readiness variables increased the explained variance by 11.6 percentage points (ΔR²=.116), showing that these factors provide important information beyond innovation attributes and UTAUT-oriented expectations. An exploratory indirect pathway was also observed: technology readiness was positively related to digital skills readiness, which was in turn related to adoption intention. The bootstrapped indirect effect was positive (ab=.067, 95% CI [.031, .108]). These findings suggest that AI-enabled cloud adoption is not only a question of perceived technological value; it also depends on whether users feel prepared, digitally capable and sufficiently confident in the cloud provider. However, all ten three-item scales showed Cronbach's alpha values below .70, and several discriminant-validity indicators were elevated. Therefore, the findings should be interpreted as data-grounded associations rather than as definitive confirmation of a latent-variable model. The main contribution of the study is a readiness-centered interpretation of AI-enabled cloud adoption in the Bangladesh context, together with a clear recommendation for future scale validation and confirmatory testing.
